Method. The finding that shapes everything else: this skill has no layer-1 checklist and no self-check section. `grep -n "checklist\|self-check" SKILL.md` matches exactly one line (SKILL.md:83) and it is prose about the posting, not a self-check. So of the doctrine's three backstop forms, the third — "a checklist item in layer 1 that names the file" — does not exist anywhere in this skill. Layer 2 here is protected only by required artifacts and deterministic checks, and there are far fewer of those than there are reference files.

And the pointer-only model is not hypothetical here — it is measured, in this skill's own harness. SKILL.md:130 says "Read `references/motivation-letter.md` and follow it." The eval-0 run recorded: "Note: `references/motivation-letter.md` was not read explicitly because this scenario's input specified no letter and the scenario context clearly did not require one" (eval-0/with_skill/run-1/outputs/RUN_NOTES.md:33). The same run then filed "Finding 4: No skill guidance on 'letter not needed' decision path for US healthcare roles" (:172) — it reported a gap in guidance it had chosen not to read. That is the slides_maker failure mode reproduced exactly: a live, well-phrased pointer, skipped, with every gate green. I weighted must_stay_inline accordingly and treated a step-level "read X" pointer as NOT a backstop.

On the renderer-docstring edge you flagged: it is not only a risk here, it is currently broken. render_letter.py:101 compares the LaTeX engine to the bare string "tectonic" where render_cv.py:992 correctly compares pathlib.Path(engine).name. On this machine find_latex_engine() returns /opt/homebrew/bin/tectonic, so I reproduced the asymmetry directly: the CV PDF built (15,927 bytes), the letter PDF failed with "LaTeX compile failed" — same engine, same invocation shape, same run. All 51 tests pass, because the one letter-PDF test monkeypatches the engine to None and never reaches that branch. The user is then told, per SKILL.md:119, to install tectonic — which is already installed. The contract that would have prevented this ("Callers detect the engine *type* from the basename") lives only in the find_latex_engine docstring, render_cv.py:751-761.

Second confirmed silent defect, and the one I would fix first: the personal-data safety interlock. references/cv-craft.md:121 asserts the renderer makes a leak physically impossible. It does not. _is_cluster1 (render_cv.py:358-360) does an exact-token lookup, and I measured DOB rendering through for 'United States of America', 'US (Boston)', 'Los Angeles, CA', 'U.K.' and 'remote (US)'. That eval passed only because the model had read cv-craft.md §2 and stripped the fields upstream (its own RUN_NOTES:22-26 says so). So the documented backstop for the highest-legal-consequence rule in the skill is load-bearing on the very layer-2 file it claims to protect against. It should move inline, and the matcher should be normalized and made to warn.

On moving this into a larger skill, the three things I would refuse to let become a reference: (a) the Step 6 review-loop block in full — verdict parsing, the all-three AND, the mandatory edit→re-render→re-judge order, the honest-gap early-stop, and the poorly-built/honest-stretch split are one interlocking mechanism, and severing any part leaves the rest looking complete; (b) the honesty stack — HONEST REFRAMING ONLY, the claim-provenance checkpoint including its third source and its re-run-in-the-loop clause, the NOT-ALLOWED enumeration, the equivalence test, and the Case-C disqualifier rule, which together are the only thing standing between a REJECT and a fabricated keyword; (c) the FIT SNAPSHOT template with its required disclaimer, which is spoken-only, artifact-free, and the single highest-consequence paragraph currently sitting unbacked in layer 2.

The extraction discipline matters more than usual here because SKILL.md:71 is already a lossy paraphrase of a layer-2 list — it silently drops salary_range and application_type from the extraction schema, and application_type is the ONLY trigger for the entire structured-application branch. That is a condensation defect that already shipped. Move lines byte-for-byte; do any genuine rewrite as a separate, small commit.

Finally, on measurement: the recorded baseline is one run per configuration despite metadata claiming three, only two of five evals have a baseline arm, and one baseline assertion is explicitly logged as non-discriminating. Treat the 88% → 100% delta as directional evidence from five scenarios, not as a stability measure — and note that the doctrine's own warning applies to any layering change made from here: content preservation is necessary and nowhere near sufficient, so the real test is re-running iteration-2 end-to-end afterwards and reading what the outputs are missing.
